title: Easy Everyday App
body: I’ve tried a lot of task management apps over the years, but Apple Reminders has become the one I rely on every day because it’s simple, fast, and surprisingly powerful. I use it for recurring daily tasks, one-time to-do items, grocery shopping, and travel packing lists, and it handles all of them without feeling complicated. The ability to create shared lists, set reminders based on time or location, and quickly add items with Siri or from any Apple device makes it incredibly convenient. Because it syncs seamlessly across my iPhone, iPad, and Mac, I always have my lists with me. It’s one of those built-in apps that’s easy to overlook, but for staying organized without a learning curve or monthly subscription, Apple Reminders is excellent.

title: Grocery list should be in notes
body: The grocery list is actually fairly useless. It’s good if you have 10 items from time to time and you need to make a little list. The whole point of computers is to save time so you should be able to save a master list as a template and highlight the items you need for each week. This list doesn’t work that way. Even if you use it as a template, as soon as you hit the button, it disappears. So in reality, it’s actually a time waster. If the master list could remain and you could highlight the items you need and then check those off while you shop that is much more in line with how people work. I also agree with others that the groceries should be in notes and not reminders. Grocery list is more of a note and not a reminder. A reminder is a singular task you need to do. It’s the Apple backwards way of thinking where you need to add a reminder for each item on a grocery list. Before computers, you took a notepad and created a note for your grocery list. It should be in Notes. Should be able to save it as a master list with the ability to highlight items needed each week. I’ve now repeated myself. Sorting items into categories automatically is cute but the list doesn’t actually function in a useful way for week to week groceries.

Demander  à Siri de Créer un rendez-vous, crée un rappel. 0 étoile encore une fois. Aprés 40 d’utilisation d’appareils Apple, je ne rachèterai plus jamais un produit Apple. Très dispendieux et beaucoup de bugs. 

Demander à Siri d'ouvrir Amazon ou Amazon Musique, Siri ne trouve pas et m’offre de chercher dans l’APp Store, je fais OUVRIR et la fois suivant même manège. J’ai essayé la prononciation française et anglaise du mot Amazon.

Demander à Siri la création d’un rendez-vous crée une minuterie sur mon ipad 9.Il y a eu même problème sur mon iphone SE pendant 10 mois.

Apple a adopté le standard USB mais a ensuite créé connecteur Lightning et nous vend un câble adaptateur de 6 pouces de long vers USB ou HDMI à $69.95 chacun. Apple a épuisé ma confiance.

Je viens de m’acheter un PC Windows $900. Une tablette Amazon Androïde  m’a couté $99. Tout fonctionne bien.

Adieu,

André Chouinard

Finally, for the Priority sorting mode, I do appreciate how it first sorts all reminders of the same priority by the earliest due date, then goes down one priority level, that's a cool touch! But then for the Due Date sorting mode, it puts the lower priorities first, going higher when down, and then the next set of reminders with the same due dates? That is weird. Overall, there are a few strange quirks here and there, but it's handy nonetheless.

title: Huge problem with the reminders
body:
Huge problem with the Upgraded reminders, the problem is spread across all my apple device when I use the reminders with icloud.

When I activate the icloud setting for the reminders on any device, for instance, my macbook, I notice the cpu start to get 100% and the reminders are not synced with icloud for 2 hours, after that, the reminders on the macbook goes well.

The same issue is going on with my other devices, on the ipad, and iphone is the same thing, except the processing time before the reminders goes well is very long, maybe 1 or 2 days, after that. reminders goes well. On my apple watch, if I activate the icloud setting on reminders on my iphone, the battery on the apple watch drain very quickly and the reminders never synced on apple watch.

The only workaround I've found is to use the reminders in local mode. I've tried many thing to get over the problem, like sign off the icloud on all device, the sign in with non result, I've done all the advises I had from apple support.
One thing I have tried have succeed, I've created a new icloud account, if a use that account, the reminders work like a charm. So this behavior sound to me the problem is directly link to my icloud account.

Lately I've do some tests on my macbook, so i've found in the library directory Library/Reminders/Container_v1/Stores a sqlite database who has the upgraded reminders. 

When I set up the icloud setting on reminders, the sqlite db start to grown slowly from 200K to 200Mo in 2 hours of processing time, while the database grown the cpu hit the 100% usage. After that the reminders are synced with the icloud account.

So, I've push my investigation more in the database, i've found in the ZREMCDOBJECT table, there is more than 57000 olds reminders (usually daily recurring reminders), after some tests, when I create a reminders, mark done and deleted it, i've notice only thing that change is the status in the table, the record is never deleted. So, as long you use the upgraded reminders, the sqlite database who support the apps is growing non stop, and someday, the database is so huge that cause performance issues with any devices who use the upgraded reminders.

This is very annoying, and I as far i’m concerned very surprising from Apple.
